newsitem.title: USA: NYNEX CEO says he has "no issue" with MCI/BT deal.
newsitem.headline: NYNEX CEO says he has "no issue" with MCI/BT deal.

text.p: NYNEX Corp's chairman and chief executive, Ivan Seidenberg, said on Wednesday he had "no issue" with the recently-announced merger between MCI Communications Corp and British Telecommunications Plc.

"BT and MCI are two very good companies. They are serious players in that they take risks, they invest new money and they create value in the industry, so I have no issue with that particular transaction," he said.
Seidenberg spoke at a press conference preceding a shareholder meeting where NYNEX holders would vote on the NYNEX merger with Bell Atlantic Corp.
"There are some details of this that we will watch very carefully," he said of the BT-MCI merger, but he would not elaborate on what those details are.
He called the latest telecommunications powerhouse a "new, refreshing competitor one has to deal with as we go forward."

He said it was only fair that the BT-MCI entity would compete with the new Bell Atlantic in the local telephone market for market share, just as the new Bell Atlantic would compete in the long-distance market.
"My view is 'come on in,'" he said. "We're ready."

On the prospect of losing market share in the newly configured global telecommunications market, Seidenberg said the new Bell Atlantic would focus on increasing revenue with new products while not losing too much market share to the competition.
"The issue for us is whether or not we are able to grow revenues faster than the loss of share," he said.
